slides.text: Your washing machine breaks. The shop tells you a new one is cheaper.
slides.footer: For years, they were right. That has just changed.

slides.text: Here is the thing about repair. We did not stop caring about it. It was quietly made awkward.
slides.footer: Spare parts priced like gold. Manuals kept in-house. Software that refuses a part it did not come with.

slides.caption: That is how much waste each of us in Ireland throws out every year, the sixth highest in the EU. A fair slice of it still worked on the way to the bin.
slides.bold: still worked on the way to the bin

slides.text: So the EU changed the default. Since last summer, if something can be fixed, the maker has to fix it when you ask.
slides.bold: the maker has to fix it when you ask
slides.footer: Free or at a fair price, and reasonably quickly. Even after your guarantee has run out.

slides.text: And it is not some obscure list. It is the stuff in your kitchen and your pocket.

slides.title: What actually changes when something breaks
bad: A part that cost more than the machine
A quote that moved every time you rang
Software blocking a part that was not theirs
good: Parts priced so repair makes sense
A written quote that holds for 30 days
No blocking a repair without a real reason

slides.text: There is a small bonus too. Choose the repair instead of the replacement and you get an extra year of guarantee on top.
slides.footer: Doing the better thing no longer costs you your cover.

slides.text: Now the bigger picture. Every device in your house is a tiny mine. Metals dug up, shipped, refined, and glued together so tightly they are nearly impossible to pull apart again.
Which is why repair is the quiet heart of the circular economy. Not recycling. Recycling is the last resort, for when everything else has failed.
slides.bold: the quiet heart of the circular economy
slides.footer: Keep it working, and nothing new has to come out of the ground at all.

slides.text: Ireland has been good at the collecting part for twenty years. It has just been counting the wrong thing: tonnes recycled, rather than things kept alive.
slides.footer: Get your phone repaired and, officially, it counts for nothing. These rules start to close that gap.

slides.text: The law changed the defaults. The rest is just us using them. So next time something packs in, look up who near you can fix it before you look up what to replace it with.
slides.bold: who near you can fix it
slides.footer: RepairMyStuff.ie is free, run by Monaghan County Council with the EPA, and it is now Ireland's official national repair platform. Search your county, pick your category, phones to fridges to furniture.
